Home » Altcoins » Binance Halts Luna Classic Burns: What’s Going On?

Terra Luna Classic’s community got used to the monthly burning ceremonies, but this time it’s postponed.

A few weeks after Binance’s $6.4 billion hack following an employee’s laptop breach, the largest digital asset exchange across the globe is resuming most of their regular services. However, the Terra Luna Classic (LUNC) community has missed the monthly LUNC burn, coming from 50% of fees garnered from Binance’s LUNC-related trading pairs.

Typically done on the first of the month, this time Binance’s LUNC burn didn’t arrive at all, chain records show. That’s the first break in a pattern running since March 2023, when Binance pledged to help restore the downtrodden Terra Luna Classic community’s hope in LUNC’s long-term restoration efforts via continuous token burns.

On-chain records show 50 batches of LUNC burns being carried out by Binance on an earlier note. The last one, which was on October 1, 2026, eliminated 335 million tokens, pushing the exchange’s cumulative Terra Luna Classic burn count towards 91 billion.

That’s roughly 19.6% of all LUNC burns to this date, a considerable contribution in the deflationary campaign.

Still no statement from @Binance regarding the monthly #LUNC burn.. Although we understand the massive hack, I feel as though a statement should at least be made to #LunaClassic investors. Is this a temporary pause or indefinite?.. pic.twitter.com/Od2yH1kFgn

Back in August, the community behind Terra Luna Classic revisited the proposal 12223 to raise the on-chain transaction tax to 1.5%. Of that, 1.2 percentage points go towards burning even more LUNC coins. Meanwhile, strong voices in the crypto community have been advocating for more exchanges beyond Binance to burn fixed-fee allocations.

KuCoin & OKX were among the ones named in negotiations. The game-tested altcoin still has a massively over-minted supply of 5.5 trillion tokens in circulation, a figure normally ascribed to meme coins.

$LUNC AND $USTC BURN UPDATE pic.twitter.com/hboLcOFNdN

However, the LUNC chain restoration efforts have torched nearly 500 billion out of the original pile, showcasing what years of strict coordination can do for an embattled community.

Aside from the 19% portion claimed by Binance, the on-chain transaction tax and direct LUNC community burns make up the rest of the historical total. Regardless, the biggest hurdle for a proper Terra Luna Classic (LUNC) restoration point remains the stagnant trading volume.

Since the hard fork in May 2022, the cumulative burn efforts crunched 6.7% of total supply so far.

Token burning is a considerable deflation measure for long-term holders to ensure the asset remains at relatively bearable market value.

Veteran trader Peter Brandt has posted an alarming warning about Bitcoin (BTC), suggesting that the world's largest cryptocurrency might never return to its previous all-time high.

In a recent post on X, Brandt shared a weekly Bitcoin chart showing what appears to be a massive head-and-shoulders formation, a technical pattern commonly associated with a bearish trend reversal.

The legendary trader's warning comes amid one of Bitcoin's worst sell-offs this year, with the cryptocurrency losing nearly half of its value since reaching its record high in October 2025.

Brandt's chart shows Bitcoin forming a left shoulder, a higher peak representing the head, and a lower right shoulder. The cryptocurrency is now testing the neckline of this potential bearish formation, located around the $60,000 to $65,000 region.

Bitcoin suffered another massive crash on Saturday, Nov. 14, extending the losses that had already shaken the cryptocurrency market earlier in the week. The flagship cryptocurrency plunged to approximately $62,830, with its weekly losses exceeding 16%.

The downturn accelerated on Nov. 13, when Bitcoin fell below the psychologically important $70,000 level for the first time since August.

The selloff was initially triggered by worsening macroeconomic conditions, particularly stronger-than-expected U.S. inflation data that increased expectations of another Federal Reserve interest rate hike in December.

Bitcoin's most recent all-time high was recorded on Oct. 6, 2025, when the cryptocurrency surged above $126,000.

That historic rally was supported by strong institutional demand, substantial inflows into U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, and the increasingly crypto-friendly regulatory scene.

#5110. Chainstack Traces Customer Data Breach to Exposed Admin Tools

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Chainstack’s expanded incident report focuses on access-control failures. Its recovery guidance makes completed credential rotation a priority.

Chainstack has added technical detail to the security incident it first disclosed on November 3. Its updated report, with a technical section dated November 10, describes an October intrusion built around configuration and access-control failures. The company says it found no evidence that a software vulnerability was exploited.

According to Chainstack, the attacker entered through a development Grafana instance with unchanged default administrator credentials. An unauthenticated tool server with broad Kubernetes permissions then formed part of the access path. Machine credentials also connected the development and production environments.

The operational lesson is about the reach of an account after the first login. A low-profile testing service can become consequential if it can contact sensitive systems or holds privileges that extend beyond its immediate job.

NewsBTC's coverage of the NEAR AI infrastructure incident explored a related boundary between an application and the services supporting it. The mechanisms differ, but both make the surrounding infrastructure relevant to a crypto platform's security.

The report identifies account names, organisation details, email addresses and password hashes as potentially exposed. It treats node credentials as exposed despite finding no evidence they were read, and asks customers to change passwords, rotate node credentials and regenerate platform API keys where used.

A password hash and a working access token create different problems. Hashes are representations of passwords, while an active token may directly authorise requests. Replacing a login password therefore cannot be assumed to invalidate every other credential associated with an application.

This is why incident guidance needs to identify the affected credential types clearly. A single instruction to change a password can leave developers uncertain about application endpoints, automated jobs and service integrations.

Chainstack's node-management documentation describes a staged rotation process. New credentials are generated while the existing ones remain active. Applications can then move to the replacements before the old credentials are deactivated.

The documentation says both sets continue working until that final step, with no automatic time limit. Completing the rotation permanently rejects requests using the previous credentials. It also says a node rotation does not change a multichain authentication token.

For an operator, the overlap reduces the risk of interrupting a working service while updating applications. The corresponding responsibility is to finish the migration. Generating a replacement alone leaves the previous means of access available.

A useful completion record would therefore track which applications have moved and when the old credentials were disabled. That is a practical control a team can verify after the initial emergency.

Grafana's security guidance warns that services on its local network may be reachable through its data-source proxy. It describes controls such as limiting permitted destinations and using firewall rules to restrict access to sensitive internal services.

Those precautions address what a tool can reach, as well as who can log into it. Authentication and network boundaries perform different jobs; permission limits provide another layer if either boundary fails.

NewsBTC's report on Chainalysis restoring screening services shows why operational recovery and data-exposure analysis can follow different timelines.

Chainstack's expanded account gives customers more detail to assess. The remaining test is whether access changes are completed and whether the revised controls can prevent one compromised service from reaching far beyond its intended role.

#5109. Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

Home » Regulations » Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

A $10.8 trillion payroll tax gap is accelerating Social Security’s 2032 shortfall—and reshaping retirement and investment strategies.

For years, the impending Social Security funding crunch has been framed as a simple demographic math problem: Baby Boomers are retiring faster than younger workers can replace them.

While an aging population plays a role, a new economic analysis reveals a far bigger, largely overlooked culprit—a structural shift in how U.S. income is earned and taxed that has quietly starved the program of $10.8 trillion and shaved a quarter-century off its solvency timeline.

According to a November 2026 study from the AARP Public Policy Institute, the program’s trust funds could have paid 100% of scheduled benefits until 2059 if the share of the U.S. economy subject to payroll taxes had simply held steady at 1983 levels.

Instead, the retirement fund is projected to deplete its reserves in late 2032, putting millions of Americans on track for automatic Social Security cuts exceeding $500 a month.

Social Security relies on payroll taxes for roughly 91% of its annual funding, according to the 2026 Social Security Trustees Report. However, a shrinking slice of U.S. economic output comes from traditional wages covered by that tax.

AARP’s analysis found that wages subject to Social Security payroll taxes accounted for 41% of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) in 1983. By 2025, that share had fallen to 34%. That 7% represents an estimated $10.8 trillion in lost tax revenue and interest between 1984 and 2034.

The report attributes this erosion to several modern economic shifts:

Under current projections from the Social Security Administration, the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) trust fund, which pays retirement and survivor benefits, will run out of reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032.

If Congress were to merge it with the separate Disability Insurance trust fund, combined reserves would last until 2034.

Depletion does not mean Social Security payments will stop entirely, because active workers will continue paying payroll taxes into the system. However, without legislative action, incoming tax revenue will only cover 78% of scheduled retirement benefits in 2032 (or 83% on a combined basis in 2034).

That translates to an automatic 22% across-the-board cut in 2032—reducing the average retiree’s monthly check by more than $500 in over half of U.S. states.

With less than six years before the 2032 deadline, lawmakers face a narrow window to either broaden how the program captures revenue from a shifting economy or let an automatic benefit reduction take effect by default.

A 22% reduction in Social Security payouts would directly compress disposable income for tens of millions of U.S. households, reshaping consumer spending, personal savings rates, and long-term fiscal deficit projections.

First, concerns about the long-term future of Social Security could lead some younger Americans to take more responsibility for their own retirement savings. For some investors, that may mean looking beyond traditional retirement accounts to alternative assets, including Bitcoin and crypto ETFs.

Second, proposals to strengthen Social Security by taxing a broader range of income could have implications for financial markets. If lawmakers eventually target investment income or adjust capital gains taxes, the changes could affect investor behavior and market liquidity across both traditional and digital asset markets.

#5107. Solo Brings Human Verification to Venmo Co-Founder’s JellyJelly App as AI Agents Beat CAPTCHA

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Solo’s SDK confirms that each JellyJelly account belongs to a real, unique person, after a Solo AI agent passed CAPTCHA on 50+ Discord servers.

Magdon-Ismail is co-founder and CEO of JellyJelly and an advisor to Solo. He co-developed the SDK behind the integration, shaping both its architecture and the way new users are onboarded.

The move comes as AI agents learn to pass the tests meant to keep them out. In an experiment run by Solo, an AI agent named Gary joined more than 50 Discord servers overnight and sent over 500 messages. No one identified it as an AI agent.

Gary had two instructions: pass every CAPTCHA challenge and accept the terms of service. It completed both through ordinary browsing and clicking, without any custom exploits.

Solo reads the result as a weakness in CAPTCHA. The challenges test whether a visitor can solve a puzzle, and capable AI agents can solve the same puzzles. Harder tests add friction for legitimate users, but they do little to show that a human is behind an account.

“CAPTCHA was built around the idea that humans could do things bots couldn’t. That’s becoming a harder assumption to make when AI agents can browse, click and solve the same challenges as people,” said Edison Siu, co-founder and CEO of Solo. “Our approach is to verify the human directly. Platforms need to know they’re dealing with a real person. Users shouldn’t have to struggle through more puzzles or upload identity documents to prove it.”

JellyJelly lets users share short videos and send cryptocurrency payments to one another. The rise of AI-generated video and automated accounts has made it harder for social platforms to know who is behind each account. Solo’s SDK brings human verification into that setting. It helps the platform tell genuine users from automated accounts, and it stops one person from registering several verified identities.

The process starts with a facial scan from a standard smartphone camera. Solo converts the scan into a biometric representation and encrypts it on the device using fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). This type of encryption lets a system work on data without ever decrypting it. Solo uses it to compare the encrypted representation against existing records, so the matching step never exposes the underlying data.

Users do not need special hardware or a government-issued ID. Raw facial images are not stored. Apps that use the SDK receive a verification result, not access to anyone’s biometric information.

The same SDK can be added to gaming platforms, payment services and other applications that need to block duplicate accounts or separate real users from automated activity.

Solo is backed by Draper Associates, the venture firm founded by Tim Draper. Draper Associates led a $1 million round in the company in March 2025. Solo was also selected for cohort 5 of the Solana Incubator.

Solo’s human verification technology is already live. The company is now working on tools that would let verified users authorize their own AI agents, so merchants and online platforms can confirm that a real, unique person stands behind each one. Solo also plans to enable AI agents and AI companies to pay verified people for work that only humans can do.

Magdon-Ismail, who co-founded Venmo and helped develop its peer-to-peer payment system, is advising Solo on how people and their AI agents will pay and get paid.

“Venmo made it easy to pay a friend,” said Magdon-Ismail. “The next step is your AI agent paying on your behalf. The business receiving that payment needs to know a real person authorized it. I’m working with Solo to make that process simple for everyone involved.”

Solo develops proof-of-humanity technology that lets online platforms check that a user is a real, unique person, without asking who that person is. Its smartphone-based system uses fully homomorphic encryption to compare encrypted biometric data, and partners receive a verification result instead of raw biometric data. Solo provides an SDK for web and mobile applications. The company is backed by Draper Associates and was selected for the Solana Incubator cohort 5. Its first product, SoloMission, lets AI agents collect feedback from verified humans.

Celestia [TIA] has had a packed month so far. Their latest breakdown of how Voyager works also has people talking.

This discussion misses the most important question though — Is TIA’s price keeping up?

In the month gone by, Celestia launched Eden, an EVM chain for testing how AI agents trade.

Fibre went live on mainnet on 20th October, adding a lane for data uploads of around 128MB, up from 8MB. On the 29th, they launched Voyager, a payments layer for AI agents.

TIA perps also got listed on Decibel on 4th November. Of all these, Voyager’s been the people’s pick so far.

In a recent blog, Blazej Kolad, Staff Protocol Engineer at Celestia, explained how it hit over 21 million TPS across 100 million accounts.

What’s surprising is that it doesn’t split the work across lots of cores. Main execution runs on a single thread.

They’re arguing that memory is the real bottleneck, and one core with the right data close by can do much and more.

There are catches, though. Voyager isn’t on mainnet yet. The benchmark skipped signature checks, and crash recovery still isn’t ready.

At the time of writing, TIA was trading at $0.40. For context, that’s an 8.7% dip over just 24 hours.

We’re a long way from mid-October. Around the time Eden launched, TIA climbed so high, it traded close to $0.76. Since then, however, it’s been dipping steadily. Now, it’s at half of that peak.

The big unlock of 31st October (which added about 5.58 million TIA to the market) didn’t help either. For most of November, TIA had been trading between $0.41 and $0.45 so far. Today though, it pierced through the bottom of that range.

The RSI was at 38.2, having briefly crossed above it on the 12th. However, that didn’t last.

Simply put, the tech’s getting all the praise. However, the token’s not reflecting any of it. Not yet.

#5105. This New AI Music Model Is Already Better Than Suno—We Put ACE to the Test

This New AI Music Model Is Already Better Than Suno—We Put ACE to the Test

Artificial intelligence has gotten pretty good at writing songs. Now, a relatively unfamiliar competitor has managed to beat Suno, arguably the biggest name in AI music, at its own game.

ACE Music v1, developed by ACE Studio, has taken first place on Artificial Analysis' vocal music leaderboard, scoring 1,160 Elo points against Suno v6's 1,144.

The AA-Music-Vocal v1.1 benchmark measures the quality of AI-generated songs containing vocals. Evaluators listen to tracks produced from identical prompts without knowing which model created them, then choose their favorite. Those preferences determine an Elo-style rating, with higher scores indicating stronger listener preference.

The lead is relatively narrow, and the models' statistical confidence intervals overlap. Suno also retains the top position on the separate instrumental music leaderboard.

ACE Studio, founded in 2018, originally focused on synthesizing singing voices from MIDI notes and lyrics. Its latest ACE Music v1 model generates complete songs from written descriptions or user-provided lyrics.

In Decrypt's hands-on tests, ACE Music consistently produced more melodic and coherent songs in mainstream styles.

That said, the vocal performances sounded more natural in general, with fewer of the synthetic artifacts that sometimes make AI singers sound like they're struggling to pronounce their own lyrics, use a lot of autotune or hallucinate words just to fill spaces. (Go ahead and give our song a listen here, which incidentally is about our latest company announcement regarding the Information Exchange.)

ACE also handled song endings better. Where Suno occasionally introduces strange sounds, unnecessary repetitions, hallucinations or abrupt musical changes near the finish, ACE generally maintained its structure and delivered cleaner conclusions.

That matters because making a convincing chorus is relatively easy compared with maintaining a musical idea throughout an entire composition even if the lyrics are already over.

Suno still had an advantage when we pushed the models toward less conventional genres.

In our melodic death metal test, ACE consistently produced tracks featuring a woman singing clearly in a pleasant, clean voice, missing the aggressive vocal delivery expected from the requested style. In general it confuses metal genres all over. Suno offered more creative arrangements in the proper heavy styles, with better stylistic consistency in several similarly demanding prompts.

The results were subjective rather than a controlled benchmark, but they showed why a leaderboard victory doesn't automatically make one model better for every musician.

ACE's most interesting feature may be its songwriting workflow.

Its “Idea” feature can develop a basic concept into lyrics and a structured composition, identifying individual song sections and describing how they should be arranged. Users can then refine the material rather than repeatedly generating completely new tracks.

The v1.1 Preview goes further, creating a musical score before generating audio.

“Each generation is a new performance, so the sound may differ even when the score stays the same,” the developers explain.

Users can edit melodies and chords, regenerate performances, export MIDI files and separate vocals from instruments for further production.

That workflow puts ACE closer to a music production assistant than a simple prompt-to-song application.

The flagship ACE Music v1 model remains closed-source with no public API, so users can only generate via the official site. However, its developers are pursuing a parallel open-source strategy.

ACE Studio and StepFun have already released ACE-Step 1.5, a separate family of models whose code and weights are publicly available. Unlike the proprietary flagship, these can run on users' own hardware—but using a weaker model.

The company also promises another release.

“We plan to open-source ACE Music v1 Flash in late 2026,” the developers state on their website, describing a version designed to balance quality, generation speed and hardware requirements.

ACE Music is available through its browser application, with a limited free tier and paid subscriptions. Commercial usage rights for flagship-model songs require a paid plan, while ACE-Step offers a separate free generation option.

For now, ACE Music v1 holds a 16-point Elo lead over Suno v6 in vocal generation. Its promised Flash release would give local users another model to try before the end of 2026.

#5103. Hyperscalers List GPUs at Nearly 2× the GPU-Cloud Price, Fluence Research Finds

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

The AI Compute Race report prices GPU compute outside the biggest buyers: a three-year commitment cuts the median price by 48%, while 17 of 22 tracked GPU models rose in price over the past year

DALLAS, Texas – November 13, 2026 – Fluence has published The AI Compute Race, a report that prices GPU cloud compute for every company that is not a frontier lab or a hyperscaler. It was produced with research partners NEAR AI, io.net, Boundless, Phala, Gensyn, Fortytwo, Theta, Compute Labs and GAIB. Its central finding: where a company buys a GPU-hour sets the price. Across H100, H200 and B200 models, hyperscalers list GPUs at 1.98 times the GPU-cloud median, from 1.4 times on the B200 to 2.8 times on the H100. The same H200 lists from $4.08 to $10.60 an hour.

Commitment length matters almost as much as provider choice. Against each provider’s own on-demand rate, a one-year reservation cuts the median price by 21% and a three-year term by 48%. Spot capacity lists at 53% of on-demand, for workloads that can be interrupted.

Buyers who expect GPU prices to fall may need to recheck their budgets. Seventeen of the 22 GPU models tracked by GetDeploying cost more than a year earlier, and the median H100 rents for 13% to 30% more, depending on the window measured.

The report also traces why prices are rapidly rising:

“Open-weight models are close behind the best closed ones, and companies are switching to them. Any company with GPUs can now serve a near-frontier model on hardware it controls. The GPUs are the hard part,” said Evgeny Ponomarev, Co-founder of Fluence.

The report closes with four ways to pay less for the same compute: compare the same chip across provider types, commit when the workload is steady, match the GPU generation to the model, and look beyond the hyperscalers, since much of the newest neocloud capacity is contracted to labs years ahead.

#5102. Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

On-chain metrics show a massive 362,000 BTC demand gap opening up across major markets.

Bitcoin crashed below the key $70,000 support level on Friday, hitting a three-month low of $67,650 as a sudden leadership crisis at Nvidia, new MSCI index rules, and hot U.S. inflation rattled global markets.

Bitcoin fell 8.6% in 24 hours to $67,650 on early Friday, its lowest mark since August 19, extending a 10.2% weekly decline.

While yesterday’s pullback below $73,000 was driven largely by macroeconomic jitters, Friday’s breakdown reflects a rare convergence of tech-sector turmoil, institutional index risks, and evaporating spot liquidity.

Adding structural pressure to crypto equities, index provider MSCI’s November Index Review has placed Bitcoin treasury companies, including Michael Saylor’s Strategy (MSTR) and Tokyo-listed Metaplanet, at risk of losing their place in major stock market indexes.

Under MSCI’s updated eligibility rules companies that hold too much of their assets in investments rather than running an operating business could lose their eligibility for indexes such as the MSCI USA and MSCI World.

When a company is dropped from a major index, funds that track it often have to sell their shares, which can drive down demand and put pressure on the stock price.

Strategy’s shares dropped 6.49% in extended trading on Thursday. The company has previously warned that eventual removal from MSCI indexes could force passive funds to sell around $2.8 billion worth of its shares.

For Bitcoin, the bigger concern is that Strategy could slow its Bitcoin purchases if it becomes harder or more expensive to raise money. That would remove a major source of buying demand just as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded five consecutive days of outflows totaling $1.43 billion, according to SoSoValue.

Market sentiment weakened further on November 12 after Nvidia announced that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was stepping down with immediate effect. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

Huang’s abrupt departure follows an internal board investigation and media reports detailing alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a alleged Chinese spy as well as relationships with Nvidia employees.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 4% on Thursday, extending a month-long decline that has wiped out 27.28% of the stock’s value. The Nvidia news added to pressure on risk assets, alongside declines in the Nasdaq Composite (-0.39%) and S&P 500 (-0.35%).

Rising inflation is adding pressure to both stock and crypto markets. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also came in higher than expected at 0.3%, against a forecast of 0.2%.

The higher-than-expected figures have reduced hopes of near-term interest rate cuts and raised expectations of a rate hike.

According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, markets are now pricing in an 88.5% chance of a 0.25-percentage-point rate increase in December. Higher interest rates could put further pressure on Bitcoin by making safer investments, such as U.S. Treasury bonds, more attractive

Blockchain data suggests Bitcoin lacked enough buying demand to defend the $70,000 level.

According to a CryptoQuant report, demand across spot and perpetual futures markets fell by 362,000 BTC over 30 days, with spot demand declining by 280,000 BTC and futures demand by 82,000 BTC.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin miner transfers to exchanges surged to 2,077 BTC on November 10, roughly 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. About 97% of the transfers came from Antpool.

At the same time, stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days, pointing to declining liquidity across the crypto market.

According to CryptoQuant analysts, the broader picture remains cautious. Leverage is being unwound, but fresh spot buying has yet to return convincingly. Until demand strengthens, ETF flows turn positive and market liquidity stabilizes, Bitcoin’s recovery is likely to remain fragile, with further downside risks still in play.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Bitcoin [BTC] closed in the red for the third consecutive day, with its price sliding to $67,000 on the charts. So far, the fall in prices has been driven by both whales and retail traders.

However, this pattern could be changing soon as Bitcoin’s sentiment starts to flip gradually. For instance, Hyperliquid whales turned back to the net long after two weeks of shorting BTC. This was the first selling period for them since March.

In fact, the daily mean of net long and net short grew from -1700 BTC on 8th November to around 900 BTC at press time. This seemed to imply that whales have been buying the dip below $70,000.

During the rally, which started in August, these whales went long. They subsequently sold the top. However, that does not guarantee that they will be right again.

On the other hand, retail traders have been showing signs of capitulation. In fact, BTC’s monthly change in Retail Investor Demand declined to around -10% after a sharp rise to over 17% as the price approached $80,000.

The same is the weakest reading since March. Back then too, Hyperliquid whales were net short on BTC.

This fall in participation by retailers, volumes below $10K, have been common during BTC’s correction.

When looking at historical patterns, it is clearly evident that when retailers capitulate, the prices tend to reverse. Thus, going against the crowd may help investors catch a move, either to the downside or the upside early enough.

Still, that does not mean that the contrarian signal always works. Even though it may be an ideal time to build positions.

This action forced leveraged traders out as supported by the sharp decline in OI. So, if BTC price stabilizes while OI stays at these levels, it would mean a rebound will be driven more by spot demand than leverage.

Therefore, whale positioning and retail capitulation could be a signal for a sustainable BTC recovery.

However, it needs to be backed by capital inflows from the market in the form of ETFs and spot buying, among others.

#5100. New Monero Privacy Update Might Be Coming Soon: Key Improvement

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Monero contributor has opened a pull request that changes how nodes relay transactions coming from Tor and I2P, according to the project's GitHub.

PR 11743 was opened on November 13 and is currently pending review. It is an updated version of a PR opened on November 8 by contributor vtnerd. After receiving feedback from another Monero developer, vtnerd, the PR was updated.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P and then passes it to the regular Monero network.

Currently, when a Monero node receives a transaction over Tor or I2P, it relays that transaction to the rest of the Monero network.

While the transaction is technically private as it travels into the node, once it reaches Monero's public peers, the transaction is no longer private. This PR proposes that Monero nodes will only accept transactions from Tor and I2P peers over incoming connections. Transactions received over outgoing Tor and I2P connections would be ignored.

Once accepted, the transaction would be subject to a random delay before being relayed to the rest of the Monero network using Monero's existing transaction relay protocol, Dandelion++. Currently, a user can instruct their node to broadcast their transaction immediately.

Over Tor and I2P connections, this request would be ignored. No transaction would be exempt from the random delay.Being able to link a transaction's timing between the anonymity network and the Monero network is an easy way to deanonymize a user. If a transaction is broadcast to the Monero network immediately after being received from Tor, an observer watching both networks can link the two.

This is a similar concept to a previous PR from vtnerd that would have introduced a randomized delay when relaying transactions from Tor and I2P to the Monero network.

While the amount of code that would need to be modified is not particularly large, this does close a hole for users that rely on Tor and I2P to obscure their location.

When the patch lands in a release is yet to be confirmed. The PR is also labeled for a backport, so it might reach the current release branch as well.

#5099. Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Send $3.6 Billion in BTC to Exchanges at a Loss

Bitcoin Short-Term Holders Send $3.6 Billion in BTC to Exchanges at a Loss

Bitcoin investors who bought recently are moving tens of thousands of coins to cryptocurrency exchanges at a loss, adding to concerns about selling pressure as the cryptocurrency falls toward the low-$70,000 range.

CryptoQuant’s latest short-term holder profit-and-loss chart shows roughly 47,300 BTC transferred to exchanges below their acquisition price over 24 hours, compared with only about 1,100 BTC arriving at a profit.

Combined inflows stood near 48,500 BTC, or around $3.6 billion at Bitcoin’s current price of approximately $74,000.

The research company's chart below shows transfers, not completed sales. Sending Bitcoin to an exchange can be the first step toward selling, but some deposits are made for trading for other tokens, collateral, or other services. The data also does not establish exactly how much of the transferred Bitcoin was subsequently sold.

The distinction is important because the chart measures the behavior of short-term holders, a group that CryptoQuant generally defines as investors holding Bitcoin for less than 155 days.

These are often the buyers most exposed to a sudden price reversal, particularly when their holdings are worth less than they paid.

In a November 11 CryptoQuant analysis, contributor Amr Taha identified two large waves of underwater exchange deposits over the previous week: 50,790 BTC on November 3 and 46,060 BTC on November 10.

“On November 10, profitable transfers stood near 1,700 BTC, meaning approximately 27 BTC arrived at a loss for every 1 BTC transferred at a profit,” Taha wrote.

That is an unusually one-sided flow. Investors moving coins into exchanges are overwhelmingly doing so at prices below those at which they acquired them, rather than cashing in gains from the earlier rally.

A similar pattern has occurred over several months, with recurring spikes in loss-making exchange transfers as Bitcoin’s price swung higher and lower. The latest red spike appears near the deepest readings visible since July.

A separate CryptoQuant chart breaks down deposits to Binance by the time since each Bitcoin last moved on-chain. It shows 3,290 BTC arriving from coins last moved one day to one week earlier on November 1, followed by a much larger 8,114 BTC from the same category on November 3.

On November 9, the platform also received 1,925 BTC from coins last moved one to three months earlier, according to Taha’s analysis. Those figures help identify which age groups are active, but they do not necessarily reveal when the owners originally purchased their Bitcoin.

The Binance chart measures one exchange and groups coins by their last on-chain movement. The profit-and-loss charts track short-term holders sending coins to exchanges more broadly.

The timing matters because Bitcoin has been sliding from its late-September highs above $85,000 into the $73,000-to-$74,000 area visible at the end of the screenshots. A newer buyer who paid $80,000 would be sitting on a paper loss of roughly 7.5% with Bitcoin at $74,000; selling at that price would lock it in.

The recent weakness is not limited to short-term holders. Glassnode identified about 4 million BTC held by longer-term investors that had been acquired between $85,000 and $118,000, potentially leaving another pocket of underwater supply above current prices.

#5097. NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

Home » Exchanges » NYSE Taps Avalanche to Power Tokenized Stock Trading as Wall Street Embraces Blockchain Infrastructure

NYSE has selected Avalanche technology to support settlement for its planned tokenized securities platform, bringing round-the-clock stock trading and faster settlement closer to reality, pending regulatory approval.

The New York Stock Exchange is mixing together blockchain technology and traditional finance. It selected Avalanche to power the settlement infrastructure of its upcoming tokenized securities platform. The decision is part of a growing effort to bring crypto trading and its benefits to traditional finance.

Announced on November 9, 2026, the partnership will see Avalanche provide the core ledger technology for the clearing firm supporting the NYSE-affiliated digital trading venue. One of the goals is to enable round-the-clock trading, as well as clearing and settlement of tokenized securities, all of which still require regulatory changes.

NYSE has organized a yearlong test, and afterwards Avalanche emerged as a favorite provider and one that could meet its needs and provide a seamless inclusion of blockchain traders into the fold of the stock exchange account holders.

The platform is designed to support equities issued across multiple blockchain networks, meaning Avalanche will not necessarily host every tokenized stock traded through the venue. The technology will therefore mostly be used to record and settle transactions.

NYSE Head of Digital Issuance Dennis Lee said that the focus was on speed, reliability, and predictable costs. Ava Labs CEO Emin Gün Sirer also highlighted the importance of dedicated infrastructure.

The crypto infrastructure industry is huge, and there’s a growing list of cryptocurrency exchanges, including those reviewed by CryptoManiaks, to choose from. Platforms made for transfers and smart contracts automating payments have also grown and now include thousands of providers. NYSE chose Avalanche due to some of its unique characteristics.

Avalanche’s architecture allows businesses to create dedicated blockchain networks with rules tailored to their operational and regulatory requirements. It creates a flexibility that traditional financial institutions are looking for.

Stock exchanges handle countless transactions, and stability is the most important feature they are looking for. Another important feature is atomic settlement. It allows the transfer of securities and corresponding payment to occur as part of the same transaction. Therefore, there’s no chance one side of a trade is completed while the other remains outstanding.

NYSE also plans to operate a custom blockchain built using Avalanche technology rather than relying directly on Avalanche’s public network.

The decision reflects a broader effort to tokenize traditional markets and get the best of both worlds. That way, crypto companies won’t dominate the space, but can combine their features with those of the stock market.

Nasdaq is among the NYSE’s most prominent competitors. It, too, has developed tokenized stock infrastructure and is pursuing partnerships that could help distribute blockchain-based securities. This is done in cooperation with Kraken and in a way that NYSE is responding to the demands of a competitive market.

The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC), a central institution in US securities settlements, also has plans to introduce tokenization. It plans to use blockchain to support securities custody and transfers.

NYSE has also expanded its list of partners. It now includes Broadridge Financial Solutions, Computershare, Equiniti, and Superstate. These developments show that financial institutions are fighting to establish the underlying infrastructure that will determine how digital securities are traded, transferred, and settled.

What Tokenized Stocks Could Mean for Investors

Tokenized stocks could change how investors are accessing traditional financial markets. The possibility of trading outside of business hours is the first thing investors have been looking for, alongside faster settlements. The NYSE’s broader platform plans include stablecoin-based funding, fractional share trading, and immediate settlement.

Ownership will also change. The NYSE has indicated that its platform will support tokenized shares that are fungible with traditionally issued securities, as well as securities originally issued in digital form. Shareholders will continue to have the same rights as traditional owners, meaning they’ll receive dividends and take part in corporate governance.

All of these benefits aren’t regulated, and before investors can take advantage of them, traditional regulatory bodies need to act and establish rules and guidelines for the new features.

Despite the institutional interest, the NYSE’s Avalanche-powered project still faces several challenges before it can become a functioning alternative to conventional securities infrastructure. The platform needs to demonstrate that it can maintain the safeguards expected of a major US stock exchange.

There’s also a distinction between Avalanche’s institutional adoption and the potential benefits for its native AVAX token. It’s not clear if the cooperation with NYSE will generate demand for AVAX. The project will depend on its ability to attract issuers, brokers, and investors while delivering reliable settlement.

At 14:48 UTC, Newhedge recorded a $260,381 Bybit BTCUSDT long liquidation at $65,571. These are individual forced closures of bullish bets, not a market-wide liquidation total or the traders' net losses.

Unlike simply holding Bitcoin, a leveraged long can be reduced or closed when a falling price erodes the collateral supporting it. A later rebound does not reopen a liquidated position.

A futures position can be liquidated when the available collateral falls below the maintenance margin required to keep it open. The system initially attempts to reduce the deficit by offloading a position into the market using an Immediate or Cancel order.

Forced closures can add selling pressure as prices fall. The records do not establish what started Saturday's selloff or how much of the decline liquidations caused.

Even a recovery to $66,000 would leave Bitcoin below the roughly $69,225 close to the week. For leveraged bulls, the immediate challenge is keeping their positions open long enough to benefit from any recovery.

#5092. Stablecoin Drain, ETF Outflows Leave Bitcoin 'Running on Empty'

Stablecoin Drain, ETF Outflows Leave Bitcoin 'Running on Empty'

The pool of dollars that fuels crypto trading is draining.

Total stablecoin supply fell by $14.2 billion over the 30 days through Nov. 9, the fastest contraction since June 2022, according to a report published Wednesday by onchain analytics firm Glassnode.

The total stablecoin supply now sits just below $280 billion, and the research company suggests that's a big reason why Bitcoin is currently "running on empty."

Stablecoins, tokens typically pegged to the U.S. dollar, serve as crypto’s cash. Traders park money in them on exchanges and onchain before buying other assets.

When the stablecoin supply shrinks, it means holders are redeeming tokens for dollars and pulling that money out of crypto entirely, which Glassnode said leaves “less fuel for a rally.” The firm said a return to supply growth would be the first sign that fresh money is coming in.

The stablecoin drain isn’t the only sign of money leaving. U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.6 billion in net redemptions over 20 trading sessions, the report found, and Bitcoin has traded at a discount on Coinbase, a gauge of U.S. demand.

Bitcoin also slipped below the average cost basis of short-term holders, about $75,600, leaving most recent buyers underwater, and traded near $73,000 on Wednesday. Over $3.6 billion in Bitcoin was recently moved over to exchanges, potentially to be sold, at a loss, according to a separate report from CryptoQuant today.

Glassnode did point to some silver linings. The slide has flushed out most leveraged long positions near the current price, buy orders outweigh sell orders in the order book, and wallets holding between 100 and 10,000 BTC have started accumulating.

The firm flagged $73,000 as key support and said the broader trend change that began in August remains intact as long as Bitcoin holds above its June low.

The contraction comes as stablecoins face growing competition from traditional finance.

Global banks including Goldman Sachs, Citi, and Deutsche Bank are backing a $270 million challenge to crypto’s dominant stablecoin issuers, and the Federal Reserve recently unveiled stablecoin rules on reserves and capital.

#5090. Telegram curbs new in-chat apps amid a no-tap hacking scare

Ordinary bots can no longer send the interactive messages. Researchers say the reported flaws affected older Telegram apps and are fixed in current builds.

Telegram has blocked ordinary bots from sending its new interactive in-message apps, known as HTML widgets, even in private chats. A November 13 reply in its Bot API repository confirmed the restriction as researchers and Telegram disputed security flaws in the feature.

Responding to a developer's report of failed widget messages, Telegram Bot API repository contributor levlam confirmed the restriction: “Yes, currently, general bots aren't allowed to use widgets even in private chats.” The developer reported receiving the error INPUT_MEDIA_WIDGET_NOT_ALLOWED after previously sending widgets successfully.

Telegram's Bot API changelog dates the introduction of HTML-widget messaging to Bot API 10.4 on November 9. The widget guide still listed private-chat production availability on November 14, despite levlam's confirmation that general bots cannot use it. The confirmation concerns HTML widgets; it does not announce a shutdown of ordinary bot messages or all bot services.

Unlike Mini Apps, which open a web page on demand, widgets run inside the message itself. Telegram's widget documentation describes an isolated environment that runs their code on the user's device without direct internet access. Requests to the bot pass through Telegram instead.

The feature has a direct wallet connection in its documented design. Telegram's changelog describes widget queries involving a user's TON wallet card, wallet-signed data or notification of a wallet transaction. Those capabilities explain the relevance for crypto users, but do not themselves demonstrate unauthorized signing or asset theft.

As of November 14, the tg-widget-rce researchers say in their research archive that its published vulnerabilities affected listed older clients and are fixed in current Telegram builds. The archive includes Android builds, Telegram for iOS 13.2, Telegram Desktop 7.4.0 and Telegram for macOS 13.1, with different findings across versions. It does not establish a definitive minimum safe version for every client.

The researchers say widget code can execute during chat layout without a tap, but delivery requires a bot permitted to send widgets and the reported vulnerabilities depend on the client build. Their technical index distinguishes app-level code execution on selected older Android builds from results contained in an isolated widget process on others. A widget-process result does not establish control of the whole device.

This rotation has historically fueled what the market calls an “altcoin season.”

What makes this particularly concerning is that the year is now approaching its end without a convincing sign of the long-awaited rotation.

Chainlink [LINK], Avalanche [AVAX], Litecoin [LTC], and Binance [BNB] also recorded smaller outflows. This suggests that investors were withdrawing capital across both Bitcoin and altcoins rather than rotating into smaller cryptocurrencies.

#5087. Nvidia-Backed CoreWeave Is Surging: Here’s What It Means for the AI Boom

Nvidia-Backed CoreWeave Is Surging: Here’s What It Means for the AI Boom

Nvidia-backed CoreWeave soared 24.7% Wednesday, helping revive the AI trade after weeks of selling, as the company reported surging demand for the expensive computing hardware powering the artificial intelligence boom.

The cloud provider posted $3.66 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 168% from a year ago, and raised its 2026 sales forecast to $13 billion to $13.3 billion. The results also helped lift Nvidia, along with AI infrastructure stocks including Nebius, IREN, Oracle and Applied Digital.

For investors watching Nvidia, CoreWeave offers a useful look at what happens after the chipmaker sells its processors.

CoreWeave buys Nvidia GPUs, installs them in data centers, and rents that computing power to companies developing or running AI models, including OpenAI and other major customers.

That makes its revenue growth evidence that businesses are still willing to pay for AI computing capacity. It does not, by itself, establish that the enormous spending required to supply that capacity will produce sustainable profits.

Nvidia's connection goes well beyond a typical supplier relationship. In January, Nvidia invested another $2 billion in CoreWeave shares at $87.20 each, expanding a business arrangement aimed at building more than five gigawatts of AI data-center capacity by 2030.

The companies also agreed to introduce new Nvidia technology across CoreWeave's infrastructure, including its Rubin platform and Vera CPUs. That makes CoreWeave an important showcase and customer for future Nvidia hardware, not just the chips already installed.

“Together, we’re racing to meet extraordinary demand for NVIDIA AI factories,” Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said when the expanded deal was announced in January.

Nvidia also has a $6.3 billion initial agreement to buy CoreWeave's unused computing capacity through April 2032, subject to the contract's conditions. In practice, the arrangement gives CoreWeave a buyer for capacity it cannot sell elsewhere, while Nvidia gets access to cloud computing built around its own chips.

The relationship explains both the excitement and some of the criticism surrounding AI investment. Nvidia sells the hardware, invests in a company buying that hardware, and has also committed to purchasing some of the computing services it helps create. Inventors call it “circular finance.” AI bros call it a meme. Skeptics call it a warning sign.

Nvidia gives money to OpenAI who gives money to Coreweave who gives money to Nvidia who gives money to OpenAi who gives money to Coreweave who gives money to OpenAi who gives money to Nvidia pic.twitter.com/3UFfK7KwJv

—  Q-Cap  (@qcapital2020) September 22, 2025

Those are real commercial agreements, but the overlapping financial relationships complicate attempts to measure independent demand.

CoreWeave reported $132.5 billion in revenue backlog, meaning contracted business that it expects to deliver over time, not money already in the bank. The company says it is working with customers including OpenAI, Cohere, and Perplexity, and had more than 1.7 gigawatts of active power capacity at the end of September.

“This was a breakout quarter for CoreWeave, with revenue increasing by more than $1 billion sequentially,” CEO Michael Intrator said in the company's earnings release.

The company also expects about $9 billion in customer prepayments and deposits over the next three months. Getting paid before delivering all the contracted services could reduce its immediate need to borrow at a time when investors have become increasingly uncomfortable with the debt financing AI data centers.

The market reaction extended beyond CoreWeave. Wednesday's rebound touched Nvidia shares and the broader technology market, with the Nasdaq gaining 1.6%. CoreWeave's report arrived as investors were trying to decide whether recent AI-stock losses reflected weakening demand or anxiety about the cost of meeting it.

These specialized GPU-rental businesses are known as neoclouds. Some—including CoreWeave, which began as an Ethereum miner—have roots in crypto infrastructure, where operators were already accustomed to running large amounts of power-hungry hardware.

Bernstein analysts described the quarter as “about the best quarter we could have asked for,” according to Reuters, but warned CoreWeave would be among the companies hit hardest if the shortage of available AI computing capacity begins to ease.

The Nvidia partnership does not remove that risk. Newer processors can make older GPUs less competitive, while electricity availability, construction delays, and higher borrowing costs can all squeeze returns. An oversupply of AI computing would also put pressure on the rental prices CoreWeave earns.

Home » Trendsetter News » XRP Exchange Balances Hit Yearly High, but Long-Term Holders Stay Put

XRP exchange balances have reached a one-year high, while the share of tokens untouched for over a year nears its annual peak.

XRP held on exchanges has reached a one-year high even as the share of coins untouched for more than a year approaches its own annual peak, according to figures cited by wealth-focused commentator Kamilah Stevenson.

Her latest video examines that split following a roughly 10% price decline, arguing that investors’ financial circumstances can matter as much as their market convictions.

On 29th October, the largest hack in crypto’s history took Bitcoin to a low near $76,200. A few days later, on 5th November, an AI-driven tech crash spilled into crypto. The Nasdaq 100 fell by 6.4%, while semiconductor stocks tumbled by 12%.

This chaos set off leveraged liquidations of roughly $1.1 billion and pushed Bitcoin’s price below $74,000.

Two different shocks, a historical Binance breach, and an AI token sell-off. Though they seem unrelated on the surface, this time they were actually the catalyst for the same event. What Bitcoin saw was a surge in speculative positioning, but what the king coin did not see was a buyer.

The market’s first take on the Binance hack was that crypto had passed a test. Bitcoin fell by about 6% from its 28th October close — a fraction of the 15% to 39% drawdowns after the controversies surrounding Celsius, FTX, BlockFi, and Bybit.

Matt Mena, Crypto Research Strategist at 21Shares, told AMBCrypto,

What we find most encouraging is how the market handled the worst of it. The largest hack in crypto’s history caused a far smaller drawdown than past crises; the protocols kept running, and none of the structural drivers broke.

Unfortunately, institutional resilience is not retail demand. The market simply treated a smaller slump as evidence of Bitcoin’s underlying strength. However, whether anyone wanted to buy Bitcoin [BTC] was a separate question, one the hack never answered.

Still, institutional strength hasn’t eased the feeling of dread felt by many retail investors. And, a major factor can explain why.

The most important signal is what happened after the liquidations: Nothing. Bitget Wallet’s analysts put it plainly that the leverage reset “has cleared some speculative excess, but is yet to address the underlying demand problem.”

Looking at the data, one can see why. Most importantly, the ETF flows changed drastically. There were $2.6 billion worth of inflows in September 2026, which turned into $290 million of net outflows in October. Currently, U.S ETF holders sit underwater below their cost basis of $82K.

How ETF holders behave below breakeven remains the key tell for November.

Also, stablecoin supply has not been moving outside the $305 billion zone, a sure sign that liquidity is sitting still.

Finally, one cannot forget the fallout caused by the Binance hack.

When the exchange reopened withdrawals, the queue moved fast. The exchange processed $4.65 billion against $1.01 billion of deposits in under ten hours; net outflows reached about $5.8 billion over 24 hours!

Each of these factors may not matter when seen separately, but when read together, they describe the same thing — capital leaving or sitting still. The leverage is gone, and the bid is not there to replace it.

For 21Shares, $73,000 is the 200-day moving average, and “the line that would reopen the bear-market debate.”

Bitget analysts told AMBCrypto that Bitcoin must hold the $73K–$74K range.

The 73,000-74,000 range is now the zone Bitcoin needs to hold. Stabilization would require more balanced derivatives positioning and sustained positive ETF flows. Reclaiming and holding $80,000 would signal stronger demand, while a decisive break below $73,000 could expose $68,000. If $68,000 also fails to hold, the selloff would suggest more than a temporary leverage flush.

When the same number pops up again and again, it stops being a coincidence and starts pointing to a pattern — that Bitcoin is either in a temporary flush or at the start of something deeper.

If buyers do return, Bitcoin can comfortably start holding $80,000, and stronger demand would emerge as a result. Getting back above $81,000 to $82,000 would finally put the largest holder cohorts back in profit.

Both reports are similarly aligned on what won’t fix Bitcoin’s buyer problem: Macro relief without demand. In fact, Bitget’s analysts asserted,

A durable Bitcoin recovery will depend on improving liquidity and Spot demand, not macro relief alone.

Matt Mena framed the same requirement as a four-part checklist.

We are watching four things into November: Bitcoin holding $76,000 to $78,000 and reclaiming $80,000 to $82,000, Binance completing withdrawals and proving its reserves, credit spreads, oil and long-end yields, and whether ETF flows return. If those turn, the setup for the final weeks of the year remains constructive.

Notice what’s on both lists: ETF flows, liquidity, Spot demand, and positioning. All of them are things buyers have to do.

There is naturally no doubt that macro factors can move Bitcoin’s price. If everything aligns, a rally can happen tomorrow. However, seasoned investors know that this will never be the same as rebuilding buyer interest.

Ultimately, a macro relief rally would leave Bitcoin’s demand problem exactly where it was.

The calendar offers a boost for Bitcoin regardless of which way the ball drops, as December’s Fed expectations hinge on U.S CPI and PPI readings. For the uninitiated, hotter readings will reinforce rate-hike expectations, and a softer core inflation will trigger a relief rally.

However, Bitget’s analysts draw a line between the two outcomes, noting,

This week’s inflation data adds another test. Hotter readings could reinforce December rate-hike expectations, while softer core inflation could trigger a relief rally. But a durable Bitcoin recovery will depend on improving liquidity and spot demand, not macro relief alone.

Basically, a relief rally can be classed as a macro event, not a demand event. The inflation print can only deliver the former, and the latter can only come about by real flows.

Here, it’s also worth being precise about what the 5th November AI crash tells us. 21Shares calls it,

A renewed wobble in artificial intelligence (AI) equities pulled the Nasdaq-100 down almost 4%.

That’s the mechanism in a nutshell. Even this time, crypto’s fall was the result of trading alongside a risk asset.

Still, if Bitcoin’s move below $74,000 was driven by the AI wipeout, then the absence of a bid is more telling. Eventually, we come back to the same problem of missing buyers.

Leverage has been reset twice in a week — Once by Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, once by an AI shocker. And the buyer bid has hardly appeared either time.

That’s what makes $73,000 a critical level to watch. If buyers return and hold this level, they could help Bitcoin reclaim $80,000. This would also imply that BTC’s demand problem is cyclical, not permanent.

However, a break below $73,000 will hint at — and a failure at $68,000 will confirm — that Bitcoin’s breakdown is structural. Bitcoin’s recovery hinges on a single level, and the lack of buyers has never been felt stronger.

#5084. Bitcoin’s oil relief has a catch: more oil at sea, less on land

The IEA raised its fourth-quarter supply forecast by 3.3 million barrels a day, while depleted land stocks and diesel shortages keep relief conditional.

The International Energy Agency raised its fourth-quarter 2026 oil supply forecast by 3.3 million barrels a day in its November 13 report and now expects a quarterly surplus. The improved outlook could reduce oil-related inflation pressure, which matters to Bitcoin through interest rates and investors' willingness to take risk.

The upgrade follows an October supply increase of 2.3 million barrels a day to 105.4 million, as Gulf exports recovered faster than demand. The IEA projects a larger inventory build in 2027. The 3.3 million figure is an increase in its supply forecast, not the size of the expected surplus.

Observed global inventories rose by 52 million barrels in October, the IEA reported. Oil on water, a component of the global total, increased by 86 million barrels, while on-land stocks continued falling and reached their lowest level since at least 2016. OECD total stocks declined by 47 million barrels.

The IEA's November outlook pairs a projected Q4 surplus with October inventory gains concentrated at sea.

The IEA raised expected Q4 2026 supply by 3.3 million barrels a day and projects a quarterly surplus.

Gulf product and LPG exports remained around half pre-war levels; European diesel was 77% above pre-war prices at the IEA's time of writing.

A stronger crude balance can coexist with scarce delivered fuel.

The 3.3 million b/d revision is not the surplus size. October stocks are observed; Q4 surplus is forecast. Diesel prices refer to IEA's writing window. No on-land stock-change amount or oil-to-Bitcoin effect is calculated.

IEA-reported stock changes and forecasts. Ship, tank and connectors are schematic, with no volume scale. Afloat stocks are part of global inventories. Selectable lenses distinguish the Q4 supply forecast from delivered-fuel conditions.

The 3.3 million b/d revision is not the surplus size. October stocks are observed; Q4 surplus is forecast. Diesel prices refer to IEA's writing window. No on-land stock-change amount or oil-to-Bitcoin effect is calculated.

That composition matters for the inflation outlook: a rising global total has yet to translate into rebuilt land-based buffers. Shipping remains a vulnerability, with the IEA warning that attacks could undermine the recovery.

Refining presents another constraint. Gulf refined-product and liquefied petroleum gas exports remained around half their pre-war levels, while attacks on Russian energy infrastructure restricted diesel supplies. At the report's time of writing, European diesel was near $180 a barrel, still 77% above pre-war levels, even as North Sea Dated crude traded around $93.

The IEA forecasts refinery runs will rebound from October's 81.3 million barrels a day to 84.7 million in December. It expects emergency diesel releases to bridge the supply gap until refinery output recovers.

Cheaper delivered fuel could help reduce inflation pressure, potentially easing one constraint on monetary policy. Broader prices still matter: the Bureau of Labor Statistics' October CPI release showed consumer prices rising 0.4%, energy 0.7% and prices excluding food and energy 0.3%, all on a seasonally adjusted monthly basis.

The Federal Reserve held its policy-rate target at 3.75% to 4% on October 28 and said inflation remained elevated. In a November 13 speech, Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said energy costs were feeding into airfares and transportation and warned about persistent broader inflation. He identified inflation's trajectory as the more important policy signal, while keeping future adjustments dependent on the data.

Bitcoin's connection runs through financial conditions and willingness to take risk. A 2023 IMF working paper found that U.S. monetary tightening reduced a common component of crypto-price movements through the risk-taking channel, resembling the effect on equities.

For Bitcoin, the potential relief depends on oil reaching refineries and cheaper fuel easing broader inflation. Rebuilt land stocks and recovering fuel exports would help; renewed shipping attacks or stubborn inflation could keep the pressure on.

Despite the market downturn, XRP Ledger is showing a somewhat reassuring trend: the price has bounced toward the $1 mark and, thankfully, the move is followed by a volume uptick, which could start a proper recovery rally.

XRP is trading at $0.96 after dipping to $0.89. The $1 threshold, which essentially enables a rapid decrease if broken, gave in on November 14. It's the first time XRP traded below $1 since mid-August.

The market is bearish, and the RSI dropped into the 20-ish zone, which is considered "extremely oversold". Moving averages are still rapidly diverging, which might further reinforce the bearish dynamic.

Even if XRP reclaims the round number, bulls might still stay sidelined. If bulls somehow wake up, a recovery toward $1.2 is the main priority, as it's the level where a lot of investors accumulated XRP in the past.

On the other hand, the Ledger shows elevated activity, with the potential to go further and reclaim levels we haven't seen in the bear market. Still, elevated activity during a prolonged market descent is not something we should just shake off.

According to on-chain data, payment volume on the XRP Ledger reached around 1.1 billion XRP, up 139.9%. Active accounts went up by 154.5%, reaching 42,300. Payments volume growth is substantial, but not record-breaking by any means.

The XRP Ledger has seen substantial growth in various on-chain metrics, which, unfortunately, does not give the price enough support. A lot of the Ledger activity might be automated, driven by either trading bots or sophisticated LLM models. The market is mostly driven by speculative interest rather than fundamental network usage.

The activity of investors who are trying to cash out or pull their holdings away from exchanges could be the key here. Growing payments volume most likely reflects growing fear among investors, as some of them move funds to exchanges in order to liquidate their coins.

Payments volume rises, but so does the bear market pressure, with a possibility of a further downturn that could make things worse than they already are.
